cls: Antineoplastic - irreversible EGFR (HER) tyrosine kinase inhibitor
pharm: Irreversibly inhibits the kinase activity of EGFR and other HER-family receptors (HER2, HER4), blocking downstream proliferative signalling in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer
quick: 45 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
Take with or without food, at about the same time each day
Can cause fetal harm; avoid in pregnancy and use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 17 days after the last dose
No adjustment for mild-moderate impairment; not studied in severe impairment/dialysis
No adjustment for mild-moderate impairment; not studied in severe impairment
No specific interaction; moderate intake advised during therapy
Pulmonary symptoms (ILD), diarrhoea, skin/rash, hepatic and general tolerability
summary: Dacomitinib is an orally administered, irreversible second-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (also inhibiting HER2 and HER4) indicated for first-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations. The dose is 45 mg once daily, taken with or without food, continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The most clinically important toxicities are interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis (which can be fatal and requires permanent discontinuation), severe diarrhoea (the most common adverse effect, requiring prompt antidiarrhoeal treatment and dose modification), and dermatologic toxicity (acneiform rash, nail and skin changes). Dose reductions (to 30 mg then 15 mg once daily) are used for toxicity. Acid-reducing drugs that raise gastric pH (notably proton pump inhibitors) reduce dacomitinib absorption and should be avoided.
indications: First-line treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer in patients with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations (as detected by an approved test)

dosage.t: With or without food, same time each day
dosage.n: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity
After recovery of the toxicity to baseline or grade <=1
Discontinue if not tolerated at 15 mg
Withhold for unexplained pulmonary symptoms; stop permanently if ILD confirmed

admin: Confirm EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutation before starting
Take one tablet once daily at about the same time, with or without food; swallow whole
If a dose is vomited or missed, do not take an extra dose - take the next dose at the scheduled time
Avoid proton pump inhibitors; if acid suppression is needed, use a local antacid (separated in time) or an H2-blocker dosed apart from dacomitinib
Start antidiarrhoeal treatment (e.g. loperamide) at the first sign of diarrhoea and maintain hydration
Use emollients and sun protection for skin; manage rash early to maintain dosing
moa: Dacomitinib is an irreversible inhibitor of the tyrosine kinase activity of the human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR/HER1) and the related HER family receptors HER2 and HER4. It covalently binds the ATP-binding site, durably blocking receptor autophosphorylation and downstream RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT signalling that drive cell proliferation and survival. In NSCLC tumours harbouring activating EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions or L858R), this inhibition suppresses tumour growth. Its pan-HER, irreversible binding distinguishes it from reversible first-generation EGFR inhibitors.

relative: Pre-existing interstitial lung disease or significant pulmonary disease
Conditions predisposing to severe diarrhoea or dehydration
Severe hepatic or renal impairment (not studied)
monitor: Respiratory symptoms suggestive of interstitial lung disease
Frequency and severity of diarrhoea and hydration status
Skin and nails for rash, paronychia and infection

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal data, dacomitinib can cause fetal harm, including embryo-fetal toxicity. It should not be used during pregnancy. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 17 days after the last dose.
lact: It is not known whether dacomitinib is present in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, women should not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 17 days after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for mild to moderate renal impairment. Dacomitinib has not been studied in severe renal impairment or in patients on dialysis, so caution is advised.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required for mild to moderate hepatic impairment. It has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment; use with caution and monitor.

major: Proton pump inhibitors - significantly reduce dacomitinib solubility/absorption and its efficacy; avoid concomitant use
CYP2D6 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index - dacomitinib inhibits CYP2D6 and can raise their levels; avoid or use with caution
moderate: H2-receptor antagonists and locally acting antacids - can reduce absorption; if needed, give antacids well separated in time and take dacomitinib several hours before/after an H2 blocker
Other agents causing diarrhoea or dermatologic toxicity - additive effects
minor: Dacomitinib metabolism involves CYP2D6 and CYP3A4; clinically significant interactions from inhibitors/inducers appear limited but caution applies
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; moderation advised
interactions.diagnostics: Requires EGFR mutation testing before use; can cause electrolyte changes from diarrhoea and elevated liver enzymes on testing

common: Acneiform rash, dry skin and pruritus
serious: Severe diarrhoea with dehydration and electrolyte disturbance
Severe dermatologic toxicity with secondary skin infection

monitoring: New or worsening pulmonary symptoms (cough, dyspnoea, fever) - evaluate promptly for ILD
Skin and nail assessment for rash, paronychia and infection
Overall tolerability to guide dose modification
counsel: Take one tablet once a day, with or without food; do not take an extra tablet if you miss one or vomit
Start anti-diarrhoea medicine at the first loose stool, drink plenty of fluids, and tell your team if diarrhoea is severe or persistent
Report any new or worsening cough, breathlessness or fever straight away - this could be a serious lung problem
Use moisturiser and sun protection; report severe or infected skin rash or painful nail folds
Do not take heartburn medicines like omeprazole/pantoprazole without checking, as they reduce how well this drug works
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed during treatment
pk: EGFR inhibition begins after absorption; clinical antitumour effect over weeks
Plasma concentrations peak about 6 hours after an oral dose
Long elimination half-life of approximately 70 hours, supporting once-daily dosing
Steady state reached in about 14 days; sustained inhibition with daily dosing
Store tablets at room temperature in the original container per label
pearls: Interstitial lung disease can be fatal - withhold for unexplained pulmonary symptoms and permanently discontinue if ILD is confirmed
Diarrhoea is the most common adverse effect - treat early with antidiarrhoeals and fluids, and reduce dose if severe
Avoid proton pump inhibitors, which substantially reduce dacomitinib absorption and efficacy
Dose reductions go 45 -> 30 -> 15 mg once daily for toxicity
It inhibits CYP2D6 - watch CYP2D6 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index
missed: If you miss a dose, do not make it up - take your next dose at the usual scheduled time. If you vomit after a dose, do not take an extra tablet; wait until the next scheduled dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for dacomitinib overdose. Overdose is likely to intensify dose-related toxicities such as diarrhoea and skin reactions. Management is supportive, with monitoring and treatment of symptoms, hydration and electrolyte correction.
